headline: Germany invades the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg
body: German forces attack the three neutral countries at dawn. Paratroopers land near The Hague and Rotterdam to seize airfields and bridges.

headline: Glider troops land on Belgian fortress
body: German airborne engineers land on top of Fort Eben-Emael, one of Europe's strongest fortifications, and disable its guns with shaped charges. The fort surrenders the next day.

headline: Churchill becomes Prime Minister
body: Neville Chamberlain resigns. That evening the King asks Winston Churchill to form a government, which will include Labour and Liberal ministers.
Woke to aircraft over the Maas. From the office window you can see parachutes. The radio says hold your positions and stay indoors. Nobody here has ever seen a war.

headline: German forces cross the Meuse at Sedan
body: After heavy air attack, German infantry and engineers force a crossing of the river. The French line begins to give way.
context: Guderian's panzer corps had moved through the Ardennes, a route French planners had judged unsuitable for armour.

headline: Churchill's first speech as Prime Minister
body: Churchill tells MPs that his aim is victory and that he has nothing to offer but hardship and sacrifice. The House approves the new government.

headline: Rotterdam city centre destroyed by bombing
body: German bombers strike the city centre while surrender talks are under way. Fires spread across the old city; around 800 to 900 people are killed and tens of thousands made homeless.

headline: Appeal for Local Defence Volunteers
body: War Secretary Anthony Eden asks men aged 17 to 65 who are not in the forces to register at police stations for a new home defence force.
context: The LDV was renamed the Home Guard in July 1940. About 250,000 men registered within the first day.

body: Heard the appeal at nine and was at the station by half past. Queue already out the door. Sixty-three and I can still read a timetable and hold a rifle. They had no forms left, so they wrote us on the back of lost-dog notices.
The office is gone. The whole street. We got out to the park and watched it burn from there. My sister is safe. I don't know about Henk.

headline: Dutch army capitulates
body: General Winkelman signs the surrender of Dutch forces in most of the country. Queen Wilhelmina and the government have gone to London.
